I changed the existing `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to run on a matrix of Node 22 and 24, so each pull request now gets two test jobs. I haven't run the workflow or checked it with a linter, because this session doesn't allow running commands.

**What changed:**
- **Versions:** the job now has `strategy.matrix.node-version: [22, 24]`, and `setup-node` uses `${{ matrix.node-version }}` instead of the fixed `24`.
- **Independent runs:** `fail-fast: false` means a failure on one Node version doesn't cancel the other, so you see results for both.
- **Job names:** each job is named `test (Node 22)` or `test (Node 24)`. If branch protection requires a check called `test`, you'll need to update it to these names.
- **Unchanged:** the actions are still pinned to the same commits, and `persist-credentials: false` and the read-only permissions are kept.

**Problem to fix:** the repository has no `package-lock.json`. `npm ci` stops with an error when there's no lockfile, so the job will fail on both Node versions before `npm test` runs. This was already the case before my change. You can fix it in either of two ways:
- Commit a lockfile by running `npm install` locally. This is the better option, but I can't do it because I can only write under `.github/`.
- Or change `npm ci` to `npm install` in the workflow. I can make that edit if you want.

**Separate note:** the "Greet" step passes the PR title through an `env` variable rather than putting it straight into the script. That's the safe way to do it, so it's fine as it is.
